## What to build

**Save project**: Exports all segments as individual .mp4 files organized into group subfolders, plus a `project.json` metadata file at the project root. The folder structure:

```
ProjectName/
├── project.json
├── Group 1 - Attacks/
│   ├── Goal_wing_attack.mp4
│   ├── Counter_attack.mp4
├── Group 2 - Defense/
│   ├── 6-0_formation.mp4
│   ├── Steal_play.mp4
└── Ungrouped/
    └── Kickoff.mp4
```

User selects a destination folder via native dialog.

**Load project**: User selects a folder containing `project.json`. The app reads metadata, finds .mp4 files in subfolders, and reconstructs segments and groups. User must re-link the source video if it is not found at the saved path (since the project is portable).

**Auto-recovery cache**: On every marker/segment change, debounce-save state to `.handball-cache.json` next to the source video. On app launch, if the same video is loaded, offer to restore the cache.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] "Save Project" exports all segments as .mp4 files in group subfolders
- [ ] `project.json` contains all metadata (segments, groups, titles, comments, ordering, speeds)
- [ ] "Load Project" opens folder picker and reconstructs full project state
- [ ] If source video path is invalid on load, user is prompted to re-link it
- [ ] `.handball-cache.json` is written on each marker/segment change (debounced to avoid I/O storm)
- [ ] On loading a video that has a cache file, user is offered to restore
- [ ] Project is portable — can be moved to another drive and loaded there

## What to build

A horizontal timeline at the bottom of the window, rendered on an HTML Canvas element for performance. Shows:

- The full video duration as a horizontal bar
- A playhead marker synced to `<video>.currentTime`
- Colored regions for each segment (showing where cuts are)
- Clicking anywhere on the timeline seeks the video to that position
- Segment regions can be dragged at their edges to adjust start/end times
- Zoom in/out controls for precision trimming on long (8-hour) videos

The Canvas approach avoids DOM performance issues with thousands of segments on long videos.

## What to build

During playback (or while paused), the user presses **I** to mark the segment start time and **O** to mark the segment end time. When both markers are set, a new segment is automatically created and added to the Pinia project store. The segment appears in the sidebar as a list item showing its time range.

After a segment is created, the in/out markers reset so the user can immediately mark the next segment.

**Ctrl+Backspace** deletes the currently selected segment.

The sidebar lists all segments with their start-end timestamps. Clicking a segment seeks the video to its start time.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Pressing I during playback/pause marks the "in" point (visible indicator on timeline)
- [ ] Pressing O marks the "out" point and auto-creates a segment
- [ ] Segment appears in sidebar with time range and default title ("Segment 1", "Segment 2", …)
- [ ] After segment creation, markers reset for the next segment
- [ ] Ctrl+Backspace deletes the selected segment from the store and sidebar
- [ ] Clicking a segment in sidebar seeks video to its start time
